name: Smartdisain Conditional Checkout Rules for WooCommerce
author: Teet Bergmann

sections.description:
Smartdisain Conditional Checkout Rules for WooCommerce lets you control the WooCommerce checkout by shipping method and shipping class, without code.

1. Checkout fields by shipping method

For each shipping method (e.g. parcel locker, courier, local pickup) you can choose:

  • fields to hide (e.g. street, city and postcode for a parcel locker);
  • fields to make required (e.g. phone number).

Fields are hidden or made required instantly when the customer changes the shipping method at checkout. A hidden field is not validated and is never required (hiding takes precedence over requiring).

The settings screen shows one card per shipping method, with a simple Default / Hide / Required choice for every field, a search box, a “configured only” filter and the option to copy rules from another shipping method.

Settings: WooCommerce → Settings → Shipping → Checkout fields.

2. Shipping methods by shipping class

A second screen shows one card per shipping class. For every shipping method choose Default (offered as usual) or Disable: a disabled method is not offered when the cart contains a product of that class. Use it, for example, to hide parcel lockers for bulky goods or to offer a courier only for fragile items.

  • Works in the classic checkout, the block-based checkout and the cart.
  • If the cart contains products of several shipping classes, a method disabled for any of them is not offered.
  • Same card layout, search and “copy rules from” as the checkout fields screen.

Settings: WooCommerce → Settings → Shipping → Shipping class rules.

3. Rules by user role

Shipping method rules per user role are in WooCommerce → Settings → Shipping → Role rules:

  • disable shipping methods (for example logged-in customers see parcel lockers but not the courier, while the role “Business customer” gets only the courier).

Payment method rules per user role are in WooCommerce → Settings → Payments → Payment rules (direct link: Plugins list → “Payment rules”):

  • disable payment methods (for example the role “Business customer” can pay with PayPal, ordinary customers cannot).

“Logged out” (guests) and “Logged in (any role)” are always listed. Roles added to your site (for example “Business customer” or a wholesale role) are listed automatically, together with the WooCommerce “Customer” role; the built-in WordPress roles are not, to keep the screen short (use the ccffw_admin_roles filter to list more). Rules of a specific role replace the “Logged in” or “Logged out” rules for users of that role: those are the fallback for everyone who has no rules of their own role. Works in the classic and the block-based checkout.

Features

  • Per-shipping-method rules for billing, shipping and order fields.
  • Per-shipping-class rules for shipping methods.
  • Per-user-role rules for shipping methods and payment methods (logged out, logged in and custom roles).
  • Block-based checkout (Store API) and classic checkout support.
  • High-Performance Order Storage (HPOS) compatible.
  • No coding needed, no external services, no tracking.
  • Translation ready: all strings are in English and use the plugin text domain, so translations can be contributed on translate.wordpress.org.

Compatibility

  • Requires WooCommerce 9.9 or newer; tested up to WooCommerce 11.2.
  • Works with the classic checkout (the [woocommerce_checkout] shortcode) and with the block-based Checkout (Store API).
  • Compatible with High-Performance Order Storage (HPOS).

Block checkout notes

The block checkout has no per-shipping-method API for its core address fields, so the plugin uses WooCommerce’s documented woocommerce_get_country_locale filter (also used for Store API validation) and reloads the checkout when a shipping choice changes the rules. Address field rules apply to the billing and shipping forms together. Email and order notes cannot be changed in the block checkout.

Privacy and licensing

The plugin is completely free, has no locked or paid features, makes no external requests, loads no third-party code and collects no data.

For developers:

  • ccffw_rules filter – modify the rules ($rules, $type = hide | require).
  • ccffw_class_rules filter – modify the shipping class rules (class slug => disabled shipping method keys).
  • ccffw_blocks_support and ccffw_blocks_reload filters – switch block checkout support or the automatic reload off.
  • A key without an instance ID (e.g. local_pickup) applies to all instances of that shipping method.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the zip: Plugins → Add New → Upload Plugin.
  2. Activate the plugin.
  3. Open WooCommerce → Settings → Shipping → Checkout fields (and Shipping class rules).
sections.faq:
Does it work with the block-based checkout?

Yes. WooCommerce does not offer conditional rules for the core address fields of the block checkout, so the plugin sets the rules on the server (the documented woocommerce_get_country_locale filter) and reloads the checkout when the selected shipping rate changes them. Rules for address fields apply to the billing and shipping forms together. You can switch the reload off with add_filter( 'ccffw_blocks_reload', '__return_false' ); or block checkout support off with add_filter( 'ccffw_blocks_support', '__return_false' );.

What happens if a field is both hidden and required?

Hiding wins. The settings screen only lets you pick one option per field.

How do I hide a shipping method for some products?

Give those products a shipping class (WooCommerce → Settings → Shipping → Classes, then the Shipping tab of the product). Then open Shipping class rules, open the card of that class and set the method to Disable.

What if all shipping methods get disabled?

The customer then sees no shipping options, as WooCommerce does when no method matches. Make sure at least one method stays available for every combination of shipping classes.

Can I disable a shipping method for products without a shipping class?

Not in the current version; rules are set per shipping class. You can filter the rules with ccffw_class_rules.

Does it work with the cart and the block-based cart?

Yes. The shipping class rules filter the shipping rates themselves, so they apply everywhere WooCommerce shows them.

Which roles can I set rules for?

Logged out visitors, all logged-in users, and every custom role of your site (for example one created by a membership or wholesale plugin). If the site has no custom roles, only “Logged out” and “Logged in” are shown. As soon as there are custom roles, the WooCommerce “Customer” role is listed as well.

How do I allow PayPal only for business customers?

Open WooCommerce → Settings → Payments → Payment rules. On the “Logged in (any role)” card set PayPal to Disable, then open the card of your business role and leave PayPal on Default. Business customers keep PayPal, every other logged-in customer does not. Set the “Logged out” card the way you want guests to be treated.

Do payment method rules also work in the block-based checkout?

Yes. A disabled payment method is removed from the available payment gateways, so it is neither shown nor accepted at checkout.

A customer has several roles. Which rules apply?

The rules of all of that customer’s roles are combined. If at least one of the roles has rules of its own, the general “Logged in (any role)” rules are not used for that customer.

Is the plugin translated?

The plugin is written in English and is fully translation ready. Translations are provided through translate.wordpress.org.
sections.changelog:
1.1.0

  • New: shipping methods by user role (Shipping → Role rules): disable shipping methods for logged out visitors, logged-in users and custom roles.
  • New: payment methods by user role (Payments → Payment rules): disable payment methods per role, with the Logged in / Logged out rules as fallback for users without rules of their own role.
  • New: ccffw_role_rules and ccffw_admin_roles filters.

1.0.0

  • Initial release.
  • Hide checkout fields or make them required depending on the selected shipping method.
  • Disable shipping methods by shipping class (WooCommerce → Settings → Shipping → Shipping class rules).
  • Support for the block-based Checkout (Store API), the classic checkout and HPOS.
  • Modern settings interface: cards, Default / Hide / Required choice, search, copying rules between methods.
  • Translation ready (text domain smartdisain-conditional-checkout-rules).

short_description: Hide or require checkout fields by shipping method, and disable shipping and payment methods by user role.
